recent_posts.title: VPP with Maglev Loadbalancing
recent_posts.summary: A deep dive into VPP's load balancer plugin using Google's Maglev consistent hashing algorithm. Covers how Maglev works (pre-computed lookup table + per-CPU flow hash LRU cache), the plugin's internal data structures (VIPs, Application Servers, new-flow table, flow hash table), and a collection of API bugs fixed in Gerrit. Two new features are introduced: per-AS weights (0–100) enabling lameduck draining and gradual canary rollouts without disrupting existing TCP sessions, and a 'punt' flag for port-based VIPs that routes non-matching traffic (ICMP, traceroute) to the local IP stack instead of dropping it. New API calls (lb_as_add_del_v2, lb_as_set_weight, lb_add_del_vip_v3, etc.) are added to expose these capabilities without breaking existing API contracts.

recent_posts.title: IPng Networks
recent_posts.summary: A deep technical exploration of SRv6 (Segment Routing for IPv6) implemented in VPP (Vector Packet Processor). Covers SRv6 fundamentals including the Segment Routing Header structure, SR Policies, Source/Transit/Endpoint nodes, and practical L2VPN configuration. The author extends VPP to support SRv6 encap/decap on sub-interfaces (not just physical interfaces), discovers and fixes a quad-loop bug in `sr_policy_rewrite_encaps_l2()` that caused ~75% packet loss when segment lists had length 1, and adds unit tests for PHY and sub-interface encap/decap scenarios. The change (~850 LOC) is submitted for upstream review on fd.io Gerrit.

recent_posts.title: IPng Networks
recent_posts.summary: VPP's policer framework has been extended to support rate limiting on VLAN sub-interfaces and L2 bridge-domain interfaces. Previously, policers only worked on physical interfaces (device-input) and L3 routed interfaces. The solution leverages VPP's L2 feature bitmap system to insert policer nodes into both l2-input and l2-output processing chains, while maintaining backward compatibility with existing L3 policer functionality. A key challenge involved correcting packet accounting to include full L2 frame overhead (Ethernet headers and VLAN tags) across all four cases: L2/L3 input/output. Comprehensive unit tests validate the implementation across routed sub-interfaces and bridge-domain configurations.

recent_posts.title: Certificate Transparency
recent_posts.summary: A detailed technical guide on setting up Certificate Transparency logs using both Sunlight and TesseraCT implementations. Covers hardware setup with Dell PowerEdge servers, ZFS storage configuration, SSL certificate management, and NGINX frontend configuration. The author shares operational experience running four CT logs (Rennet, Lipase, Gouda, and Halloumi) with specific focus on security, redundancy, and performance considerations including ECC memory, encrypted storage, and distributed frontend architecture.

recent_posts.title: Certificate Transparency
recent_posts.summary: Sunlight is a Certificate Transparency log implementation designed for scalability and ease of operation. Performance testing shows Sunlight can handle up to 5,000 certificates per second with S3 backend and around 4,400/s with POSIX filesystem, making it more efficient with S3 storage than TesseraCT but slightly slower on local storage. The implementation features built-in Prometheus metrics, supports multiple logs in one configuration, and uses SQLite for local caching, reducing operational complexity compared to alternatives.

recent_posts.title: IPng Networks
recent_posts.summary: Technical documentation showing Cisco IOS XR configuration examples for L2VPN services, including L2 point-to-point cross-connects and bridge domains. Demonstrates interface configurations with 10GigE ports, MAC address forwarding tables, and MPLS static label configurations. Highlights a critical finding where bridge domain overload causes forwarding to stop, with traffic statistics showing asymmetric input/output patterns across interfaces.

recent_posts.title: VPP and eVPN/VxLAN
recent_posts.summary: VPP (Vector Packet Processing) currently supports point-to-point VxLAN tunnels but lacks dynamic EVPN capabilities for multi-site L2 domains. The author proposes extending VPP with dynamic VxLAN functionality that includes per-interface L2FIB tables and flood lists, enabling EVPN/VxLAN speaker capabilities. This would solve the scalability issues of current full-mesh VxLAN configurations by implementing BGP EVPN control plane integration, similar to how route reflectors solve iBGP scaling problems. The proposal includes API designs, prototype implementation details, and demonstrates the concept with working code examples.

recent_posts.title: Case Study: Minio S3
recent_posts.summary: A detailed implementation guide showing how to deploy MinIO S3-compatible object storage for backup and web asset serving. Covers setting up Restic backups with S3 backend, configuring bucket replication between MinIO instances for redundancy, and implementing NGINX proxy caching to serve static assets from S3 storage with significant performance improvements.

recent_posts.title: Case Study: Minio S3
recent_posts.summary: A detailed technical walkthrough of setting up a distributed MinIO S3-compatible object storage system across three Dell R720 servers with 192TB of storage each. The implementation covers hardware preparation, disk formatting with XFS, MinIO configuration with erasure coding, NGINX reverse proxy setup with Let's Encrypt certificates, and monitoring integration with Prometheus and Nagios. The author demonstrates creating buckets, setting permissions, and achieving high-performance data transfers while maintaining geographical distribution across multiple data centers.

recent_posts.title: VPP in Containerlab
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses integrating a Vector Packet Processing (VPP) environment within the Containerlab framework. It starts by exploring how to package VPP within a Docker container, and then delves into setting up VPP in a Containerlab environment using various configurations such as network namespaces, SSH setups, Bird2 configurations, and interface bindings. The process includes demoing a VPP setup in Containerlab with example configurations for networking labs.

top_posts.title: FrysIX eVPN: think different
top_posts.summary: FrysIX, located in the Netherlands, has been successfully operating and expanding since 2021. With the traffic reaching 800Gbps, the network leveraged Nokia 7220 Interconnect Routers for better scalability and flexibility. An eVPN-based demo topology was implemented to overcome limitations in traditional designs like Clos networks. Essential configurations included the use of Nokia's SR Linux and Arista switches with VXLAN and BGP EVPN for efficient data routing and peering. Future improvements involve port security, ARP suppression, and automation for enhanced resilience.

top_posts.title: VPP with sFlow
top_posts.summary: The post explores the implementation of the sFlow protocol with Vector Packet Processing (VPP) primarily for anti-DDoS protection and network monitoring. It details collaboration with experts, discusses the architecture and performance of the sFlow plugin, and outlines configuration steps and testing results. The article highlights both the challenges and successes encountered, including performance metrics and troubleshooting experiences.

top_posts.title: Case Study: NAT64
top_posts.summary: The post discusses the implementation of NAT64, Jool, and DNS64 for IPv6-only clients to access IPv4 servers. It describes the setup of border gateways with firewalling and NAT translation capabilities. The post also explains the role of DNS64 in synthesizing AAAA records from A records.

top_posts.title: VPP with Babel - Part 1
top_posts.summary: This post explores the use of VPP and Babel to conserve IPv4 addresses and introduces the concept of unnumbered interfaces in VPP.
